body.statement: Assign unit cost to every vertex of \(G_H\). Every vertex cover \(C\subseteq U\) maps to the intervention \(\{x_u:u\in C\}\) with the same cost, and every feasible intervention maps in polynomial time, by replacing each selected \(z_e\) with an endpoint of \(e\), to a vertex cover of no larger cost. Therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\). The reduction is an \(L\)-reduction with constants one, so rank-three MCID is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard even with unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree; the \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness remains for source graphs of maximum degree three.
body.justification: Objective preservation identifies the exact complexity transition at the first nonempty rank rather than importing generic three-hitting-set hardness.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove unrestricted MCID hardness, while Alimonti and Kann supply cubic vertex-cover hardness; neither gives a promise-preserving rank-three causal realization.
body.consumer: The result supplies structured hard instances on which the RC2 and Gurobi formulations can be evaluated without uncontrolled hedge rank.
body.proof_tex:
Assign \(c(v)=1\) to every \(v\in V^{-}\).  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) identifies the
minimal residual clutter of \(G_H\) as
\[
 \mathcal C(G_H,s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E\bigr\}.
\]
Thus the constraint indexed by \(e=\{u,v\}\) is precisely
\[
 A\cap\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\neq\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, by Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) and its hedge-hitting
identification bridge, these are exactly the interventions for which the
acquired proxy law identifies the causal target \(Q_s\).

Let \(C\subseteq U\) be a vertex cover of \(H\) and put
\[
 A_C=\{x_u:u\in C\}.
\]
For every \(e=\{u,v\}\in E\), at least one of \(u,v\) belongs to \(C\), so
\(A_C\) meets \(\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\).  Hence \(A_C\) is feasible and, because
all costs are one,
\[
 c(A_C)=\sum_{w\in A_C}c(w)=|C|.
\]
Minimizing over vertex covers gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\leq\tau(H).
\]

Conversely, let \(A\subseteq V^{-}\) be any feasible intervention and begin
with
\[
 C_0=\{u\in U:x_u\in A\}.
\]
Process the edges in any fixed order.  Whenever an edge
\(e=\{u,v\}\) is not covered by the current set, insert one of its endpoints
(for definiteness, the \(\prec\)-smaller endpoint).  Feasibility implies
that \(z_e\in A\) whenever this insertion is required: indeed, neither
\(x_u\) nor \(x_v\) then belongs to \(A\), and the constraint
\(A\cap\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\neq\varnothing\) forces \(z_e\in A\).  Associate the
insertion with this private guard.  Distinct processed edges have distinct
guards, and insertions that repeat an already inserted endpoint only reduce
the final cardinality.  The resulting set \(C_A\) covers every edge and
satisfies
\[
 |C_A|
 \leq |\{u:x_u\in A\}|+|\{e:z_e\in A\}|
 =|A|.
\]
The last equality uses the construction of \(G_H\), whose manipulable
vertices are exactly the source copies and private guards.  Applying this
map to an optimal intervention yields
\[
 \tau(H)\leq |C_A|\leq |A|=\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c).
\]
Together with the preceding upper bound, this proves
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H).
\]

We finally verify the approximation-preserving constants.  The forward map
\(H\mapsto G_H\) has
\(1+|U|+|E|\) vertices and is computable in polynomial time, and the reverse
replacement map just described is polynomial.  Equality of the optima gives
the first \(L\)-reduction inequality with \(\alpha=1\):
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\leq \tau(H).
\]
Since every \(C_A\) is a vertex cover, \(|C_A|\geq\tau(H)\); combining this
with \(|C_A|\leq|A|\) and equality of the optima gives
\[
 0\leq |C_A|-\tau(H)
 \leq |A|-\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c),
\]
which is the second \(L\)-reduction inequality with \(\beta=1\).
Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}cubic\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}apx\mbox{-}complete}\)
states that Minimum Vertex Cover is \(\mathsf{APX}\)-complete, and hence
\(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard, even when the source graph
has maximum degree at most three.  The unit-constant \(L\)-reduction
transfers both hardness conclusions.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) supplies, for
every such source instance, residual rank three (when \(E\neq\varnothing\))
and a bidirected tree of radius at most two.  This proves every claimed
restriction.  If exact rank three rather than the promise \(r\leq3\) is
requested, edgeless source instances are recognized and solved trivially;
on every remaining instance \(E\neq\varnothing\), so the same reduction
has rank exactly three.
